When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

5	missing state file is created on first use; a corrupted file or a document
6	whose version is not understood makes the server refuse to start (state is
7	never silently discarded). Every change is a *two-file atomic transaction*:
8	the new state document and the sidecar with the generation's new entry are
9	serialized to sibling temporary files (``.state-*.tmp`` /
10	``.integrity-*.tmp``) in the same directory and ``fsync``-ed, hard-link
11	backups of both current targets are taken when they exist
12	(``.state-*.bak`` / ``.integrity-*.bak``), both temporaries are
13	``os.replace``-d over their targets, and the parent directory is fsynced
14	once, so a crash always leaves a matched, hash-chain-consistent pair and
15	never a torn mix. The pair is only committed when both files are of the
16	same generation and the sidecar tail's ``state_hash`` binds that
17	generation's canonical state; each successful transaction raises the
18	generation by exactly one.
19	
20	Persistence is transactional with respect to the in-memory store: the change
21	hook fires while the store lock is held (the mutation is visible but not yet
22	committed to callers). When the durable write succeeds it becomes the new
23	last-known-good pair. When writing either temporary file, fsync-ing either
24	file, or either atomic replace fails (an :class:`OSError`), the previous
25	last-known-good pair is restored under the same lock and
26	:class:`PersistenceUnavailable` is raised so the HTTP layer answers
27	503/field=data_file; the failed mutation therefore never advances either
28	memory or either file. A platform/filesystem that cannot fsync a directory
29	skips that one capability instead of failing the transaction (the file
30	fsyncs and the atomic renames already landed); genuine I/O errors still
31	roll the transaction back.
32	
33	After both replaces have landed, a failed directory fsync first rolls the
34	transaction back symmetrically: each pinned old inode is renamed over its
35	formal target and a second directory fsync flushes the rollback. When that
36	rollback itself cannot be completed durably — a rollback rename fails, or
37	the second fsync fails — the failure stays *decidable*: both old inodes are
38	kept under their paired ``.state-*.bak`` / ``.integrity-*.bak`` backups and
39	both un-committed snapshots are taken off their formal paths (the new state
40	snapshot is parked under a ``.quarantine`` name the recovery scan never
41	promotes, or deleted; the un-committed sidecar is deleted), so *both*
42	formal paths are missing. The store is then marked degraded and reports 503
43	for the failed request.
44	
45	The degraded store also heals itself *within the same process*: the next
46	persist-able write runs, inside the storage lock, :meth:`JsonStateStore.heal`
47	before saving — a unique *pair* of pinned backups is fully verified (the
48	state backup at the previous generation with version=1 semantics and exact
49	equality with the last committed in-memory state, and the sidecar backup
50	with a complete hash chain whose tail binds that generation and state hash),
51	both are hard-linked back onto their formal paths, same-transaction
52	leftovers (``.quarantine``/``.tmp``/redundant ``.bak`` on either file) are
53	removed, and only then is that one triggering request committed (a single
54	consecutive ``commit_seq`` advance). The request that originally got 503 is
55	never replayed; the healed commit carries only the later, current request.
56	A corrupt, dangling, unpaired or ambiguous backup is refused promotion: the
57	request gets 503/field=data_file, memory is rolled back, both formal paths
58	stay missing, no leftover and no generation moves, and the next write
59	retries the heal. A valid formal pair always takes precedence over every
60	backup. Restart recovery remains the fallback that promotes the pinned
61	pair.
62	
63	When even the decidable fallback cannot be achieved — one formal path
64	(typically the state file) cannot be proven missing, so an un-committed
65	snapshot may still occupy it while the committed inode survives only in a
66	backup — the store enters the *blocking state* (a sibling
67	``.state-*.block`` marker persists it across restarts). It never serves
68	that residual formal file as authoritative: every subsequent write is
69	503/field=data_file, in this process and after a restart, until the path is
70	vacated with exactly one verifiable backup pair (heal/restart then promote
71	it and clear the marker), or files provably equal to the committed state
72	are restored onto both formal paths (a valid formal pair always wins). Two
73	or more verifiable state backups make a pair ambiguous even against one
74	sidecar backup and are refused rather than picked by name or mtime.
75	
76	A crash between steps can leave ``.state-*.tmp``/``.state-*.bak`` and
77	``.integrity-*.tmp``/``.integrity-*.bak`` files beside the targets. At the
78	next :func:`attach_persistence` these are resolved by
79	:func:`recover_crash_leftovers`: a valid matched formal pair stays
80	authoritative and every leftover is removed; with the state file missing,
81	state leftovers and sidecar leftovers are combined into *pairs* and only a
82	pair that passes version=1 semantics, carries the complete-transaction
83	sections, has a valid sidecar chain whose tail generation and
84	``state_hash`` bind the state document (or, for a legacy document without
85	the integrity marker, has no sidecar at all) is considered; the pair at the
86	highest generation is recovered atomically (modification time breaks ties
87	only between genuinely pre-generation files). Verifiable candidates
88	without a unique pair make startup raise :class:`StateFileError` (exit 1,
89	one stderr JSON line, field=data_file) with nothing deleted or overwritten;
90	only when no candidate is verifiable are the leftovers removed and an empty
91	state created. An existing-but-corrupt formal file still makes startup
92	refuse rather than being silently overwritten; a legacy version=1 state
93	file without the marker and without a sidecar keeps loading as before.
94	
95	Every document carries a strictly-consecutive top-level ``commit_seq``: the
96	first empty state is written at 0 and each successful durable transaction
97	advances it exactly once (a failed write consumes no generation). A legacy
98	version=1 file without the field loads as generation 0; a present field must
99	be a non-negative integer or startup refuses (bool, negative, float and
100	string values are rejected) with the file untouched.
101	
102	Beside the state file every normal commit maintains the append-only
103	integrity sidecar at ``<state>.integrity`` (a compact version=1 JSON
104	document with one ``commit_seq``/``state_hash``/``prev_hash``/``hash``
105	entry per committed generation), written in the same locked two-file
106	transaction. The sidecar document's key order is ``version`` then
107	``entries`` and each entry keeps
108	``commit_seq``/``state_hash``/``prev_hash``/``hash`` order; both files are
109	UTF-8, ``ensure_ascii=False``, compact JSON with no whitespace or trailing
110	newline. The state document records the format with
111	``integrity_log_version=1``; a legacy file without that marker and without
112	a sidecar still starts and anchors the chain on its first commit, while any
113	marker/sidecar disagreement or a broken / tail-mismatched chain makes
114	startup refuse with both files untouched. The sidecar backs
115	``GET /v1/persistence/integrity/history`` and its ascending, cursor-paged
116	variant ``GET /v1/persistence/integrity/history/page``
117	(``commit_seq > after``, at most ``limit``).
118	"""

142	#: Integrity sidecar log format version.
143	INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION = 1

146	INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY = "integrity_log_version"

153	_TMP_SUFFIX = ".tmp"
154	#: Suffix of the pre-replace hard-link backup pinning the previous inode.
155	_BAK_SUFFIX = ".bak"
156	#: Name parts of the integrity sidecar's own staging files and pinned-inode
157	#: backups: every commit stages and pins *both* formal files through the same
158	#: two-file transaction, so crash leftovers and backups come in pairs
159	#: (``.state-*`` beside ``.integrity-*``).
160	_INTEGRITY_TMP_PREFIX = ".integrity-"
161	_INTEGRITY_TMP_SUFFIX = ".tmp"
162	_INTEGRITY_BAK_SUFFIX = ".bak"
163	#: Suffix of a new snapshot taken off the formal path when the rollback
164	#: itself cannot be completed durably. Such a file is deliberately *not* a
165	#: crash-recovery candidate (the scan only promotes ``.tmp``/``.bak``): the
166	#: transaction it staged was already reported failed and rolled back in
167	#: memory, so it must never be resurrected at the next startup.
168	_QUARANTINE_SUFFIX = ".quarantine"
169	#: Suffix of the durable marker left when a failed transaction could not be made
170	#: decidable: the formal path could not be vacated, so a possibly-un-committed
171	#: residual formal file sits beside a ``.bak`` of the last committed
172	#: inode. While such a marker exists the store is in the *blocking state*:
173	#: writes are refused (503/field=data_file) and the residual formal file is
174	#: never treated as authoritative, until an operator removes the marker (after resolving
175	#: the on-disk state) — or until heal finds the formal path missing with
176	#: exactly one verifiable backup, at which point it clears the marker itself.
177	_BLOCK_SUFFIX = ".block"

180	#: writes a document whose ``commit_seq`` is exactly one higher than the
181	#: previous one; the first (empty) state is created at 0. A legacy version-1
182	#: file written before this field loads as if it carried 0.
183	COMMIT_SEQ_KEY = "commit_seq"

186	def _valid_commit_seq(value: Any) -> bool:
187	    """A commit generation is a non-negative JSON integer (never a bool)."""
188	    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value >= 0

191	def _commit_seq_of(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> int:
192	    """Rank a candidate by its commit generation; a missing/malformed one is 0.

194	    Leftover snapshots are ranked leniently here (a leftover without the field
195	    predates commit generations and sorts at generation 0); the *formal*
196	    file's field is validated strictly by :meth:`JsonStateStore.load`.
197	    """
198	    value = document.get(COMMIT_SEQ_KEY, 0)
199	    return value if _valid_commit_seq(value) else 0

227	class IntegrityLogError(Exception):
228	    """The integrity-history sidecar is missing or fails every check.
229	
230	    Raised at startup when the ``integrity_log_version`` marker and the
231	    sibling ``<state>.integrity`` log disagree (one present without the
232	    other, or an unknown marker value), or when the log document is
233	    structurally invalid, its hash chain is broken, an entry hash does not
234	    verify, or its last entry does not match the state file's generation.
235	    The store refuses to start and leaves both files untouched.
236	    """
237	
238	
239	def _integrity_entry_hash(commit_seq: int, state_hash: str,
240	                          prev_hash: str) -> str:
241	    """Hash one integrity-log entry: the entry without ``hash``.
242	
243	    Keys are sorted, separators compact and Unicode written literally; the
244	    UTF-8 bytes are SHA-256 digested to lowercase hex, exactly like the
245	    key-audit event chain.
246	    """
247	    document = {"commit_seq": commit_seq, "state_hash": state_hash,
248	                "prev_hash": prev_hash}
249	    canonical = json.dumps(document, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"),
250	                           ensure_ascii=False)
251	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
252	
253	
254	def _is_hex64(value: Any) -> bool:
255	    return isinstance(value, str) and len(value) == 64 \
256	        and all(ch in "0123456789abcdef" for ch in value)
257	
258	
259	def _read_integrity_log(path: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
260	    """Parse the integrity sidecar, or ``None`` when it does not exist.
261	
262	    Returns the raw parsed document (validation happens in
263	    :func:`_verify_integrity_log`). Unreadable/undecodable files raise
264	    :class:`IntegrityLogError` rather than returning ``None``: only a
265	    genuinely absent file means "no sidecar".
266	    """
267	    try:
268	        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
269	            raw = handle.read()
270	    except FileNotFoundError:
271	        return None
272	    except OSError as error:
273	        raise IntegrityLogError(
274	            f"cannot read integrity log {path}: {error}") from None
275	    try:
276	        document = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
277	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
278	        raise IntegrityLogError(
279	            f"integrity log is not valid JSON: {path} ({error})") from None
280	    if not isinstance(document, dict):
281	        raise IntegrityLogError("integrity log must be a JSON object")
282	    return document
283	
284	
285	def _verify_integrity_log(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
286	    """Fully validate a parsed integrity sidecar; return its entries.
287	
288	    Enforces top-level shape (``version == 1``, an ``entries`` list, no
289	    extra keys), each entry's shape and key order, strictly-consecutive
290	    ``commit_seq`` values in ascending order, lowercase-hex hashes, an empty
291	    ``prev_hash`` on the first entry chained to the previous ``hash`` on
292	    every later one, and that each entry's ``hash`` is the SHA-256 of its
293	    ``commit_seq``/``state_hash``/``prev_hash`` (sorted-key compact JSON).
294	
295	    The first entry may carry any non-negative generation: a legacy file
296	    loaded without a sidecar anchors the chain at the generation of the
297	    first write that enables it; every later entry is exactly one
298	    generation higher. Binding of the chain *tail* to the state file's
299	    current generation and hash is the caller's last-entry check.
300	    Raises :class:`IntegrityLogError` on the first violation.
301	    """
302	    if list(document) != ["version", "entries"]:
303	        raise IntegrityLogError(
304	            "integrity log must have exactly the keys 'version' and "
305	            "'entries' in order")
306	    version = document.get("version")
307	    if not isinstance(version, int) or isinstance(version, bool):
308	        raise IntegrityLogError("integrity log is missing a numeric version")
309	    if version != INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION:
310	        raise IntegrityLogError(
311	            f"unsupported integrity log version: {version} "
312	            f"(this server supports {INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION})")
313	    entries = document.get("entries")
314	    if not isinstance(entries, list):
315	        raise IntegrityLogError("integrity log 'entries' must be a list")
316	    verified: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
317	    prev_hash = ""
318	    anchor_seq: Optional[int] = None
319	    for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
320	        where = f"integrity log entries[{index}]"
321	        if not isinstance(entry, dict):
322	            raise IntegrityLogError(f"{where} must be an object")
323	        if list(entry) != ["commit_seq", "state_hash", "prev_hash", "hash"]:
324	            raise IntegrityLogError(
325	                f"{where} must have exactly the keys 'commit_seq', "
326	                f"'state_hash', 'prev_hash', 'hash' in order")
327	        commit_seq = entry["commit_seq"]
328	        state_hash = entry["state_hash"]
329	        entry_prev = entry["prev_hash"]
330	        entry_hash = entry["hash"]
331	        if not isinstance(commit_seq, int) or isinstance(commit_seq, bool) \
332	                or commit_seq < 0:
333	            raise IntegrityLogError(
334	                f"{where}.commit_seq must be a non-negative integer")
335	        if not _is_hex64(state_hash):
336	            raise IntegrityLogError(
337	                f"{where}.state_hash must be a 64-character lowercase hex "
338	                f"string")
339	        if not isinstance(entry_prev, str):
340	            raise IntegrityLogError(f"{where}.prev_hash must be a string")
341	        if not _is_hex64(entry_hash):
342	            raise IntegrityLogError(
343	                f"{where}.hash must be a 64-character lowercase hex string")
344	        if index == 0:
345	            anchor_seq = commit_seq
346	            if entry_prev != "":
347	                raise IntegrityLogError(
348	                    "integrity log first entry must have an empty prev_hash")
349	        else:
350	            expected_seq = anchor_seq + index
351	            if commit_seq != expected_seq:
352	                raise IntegrityLogError(
353	                    "integrity log commit_seq values must be ascending and "
354	                    f"consecutive: entries[{index}] carries {commit_seq}, "
355	                    f"expected {expected_seq}")
356	            if entry_prev != prev_hash:
357	                raise IntegrityLogError(
358	                    f"integrity log has a broken prev_hash link at "
359	                    f"entries[{index}]")
360	        expected_hash = _integrity_entry_hash(
361	            commit_seq, state_hash, entry_prev)
362	        if entry_hash != expected_hash:
363	            raise IntegrityLogError(
364	                f"integrity log entry hash mismatch at entries[{index}]")
365	        prev_hash = entry_hash
366	        verified.append({"commit_seq": commit_seq, "state_hash": state_hash,
367	                         "prev_hash": entry_prev, "hash": entry_hash})
368	    return verified

372	    """Read and fully validate the sidecar at *path* (``None`` if absent)."""
373	    document = _read_integrity_log(path)

379	def _serialize_integrity_log(entries: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> bytes:
380	    """Serialize the whole sidecar as compact, key-ordered UTF-8 JSON.
381	
382	    Top-level key order is ``version`` then ``entries``; each entry keeps
383	    ``commit_seq``/``state_hash``/``prev_hash``/``hash`` order. No
384	    whitespace and ``ensure_ascii=False`` match the hashed representation.
385	    """
386	    document = {"version": INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION, "entries": entries}
387	    return json.dumps(document, separators=(",", ":"),
388	                      ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")

391	def _sidecar_leftover_paths(directory: str,
392	                            target_path: str) -> List[str]:
393	    """List crashed sidecar files: ``.integrity-*.tmp``/``.integrity-*.bak``.
394	
395	    The authoritative sidecar (``<state>.integrity``) is never listed. Both
396	    staging snapshots (``.tmp``) and pinned inode backups (``.bak``) are
397	    pairing candidates; validity is decided later, never by suffix alone.
398	    """
399	    try:
400	        names = os.listdir(directory)
401	    except OSError:
402	        return []
403	    leftovers: List[str] = []
404	    for name in names:
405	        if not name.startswith(_INTEGRITY_TMP_PREFIX):
406	            continue
407	        if not (name.endswith(_INTEGRITY_TMP_SUFFIX)
408	                or name.endswith(_INTEGRITY_BAK_SUFFIX)):
409	            continue
410	        full = os.path.join(directory, name)
411	        if os.path.abspath(full) == os.path.abspath(target_path):
412	            continue
413	        leftovers.append(full)
414	    return leftovers

437	def _state_document_state_hash(document: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
438	    """Canonical ``state_hash`` of a version-1 state document's payload.
439	
440	    Strips the envelope (``version``/``commit_seq``/
441	    ``integrity_log_version``), restores the payload into a fresh store and
442	    hashes its canonical snapshot — the same round trip the startup marker
443	    gate uses to bind a sidecar tail. Returns ``None`` when the payload does
444	    not restore.
445	    """
446	    payload = {key: value for key, value in document.items()
447	               if key not in ("version", COMMIT_SEQ_KEY,
448	                              INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY)}
449	    try:
450	        fresh = DeviceStore()
451	        fresh.restore_state(copy.deepcopy(payload))
452	        canonical = canonical_integrity_snapshot(fresh.snapshot_state())
453	    except (ValueError, TypeError):
454	        return None
455	    return integrity_state_hash(canonical)

458	def _sidecar_tail_binds(entries: List[Dict[str, Any]], seq: int,
459	                        state_hash: str) -> bool:
460	    """Whether a verified sidecar's tail binds generation *seq*/*state_hash*."""
461	    if not entries:
462	        return False
463	    last = entries[-1]
464	    return last["commit_seq"] == seq and last["state_hash"] == state_hash

467	class RecoveryPair:
468	    """One state candidate paired with the sidecar that binds its tail.
469	
470	    ``sidecar_path`` is ``None`` for a legacy, marker-less state with no
471	    sidecar at all. The ``*_is_formal`` flags distinguish a file already on a
472	    formal path from a leftover pin/staged snapshot.
473	    """
474	
475	    __slots__ = ("state_path", "sidecar_path", "state_is_formal",
476	                 "sidecar_is_formal", "commit_seq", "has_seq", "mtime_ns")
477	
478	    def __init__(self, state_path: str, sidecar_path: Optional[str],
479	                 state_is_formal: bool, sidecar_is_formal: bool,
480	                 commit_seq: int, has_seq: bool, mtime_ns: int) -> None:
481	        self.state_path = state_path
482	        self.sidecar_path = sidecar_path
483	        self.state_is_formal = state_is_formal
484	        self.sidecar_is_formal = sidecar_is_formal
485	        self.commit_seq = commit_seq
486	        self.has_seq = has_seq
487	        self.mtime_ns = mtime_ns
488	
489	
490	def _pair_state_sidecar_candidates(
491	        state_cands: List[Tuple[str, Dict[str, Any], bool]],
492	        sidecar_cands: List[Tuple[str, List[Dict[str, Any]], bool]],
493	        formal_sidecar_present: bool
494	) -> List[RecoveryPair]:
495	    """Combine verified state and sidecar candidates into verifiable pairs.
496	
497	    A marker-less *legacy* state candidate pairs (with ``sidecar_path``
498	    ``None``) only while no *formal* sidecar sits beside it — the existing
499	    missing-sidecar compatibility; any sidecar crash leftovers
500	    (``.integrity-*.tmp``/``.bak``) are unrelated garbage the caller sweeps
501	    after promoting the legacy state (a surviving formal sidecar beside a
502	    marker-less state is the strict startup gate's disagreement). A
503	    marker-stamped candidate pairs with every sidecar candidate whose
504	    verified tail binds the state document's generation and canonical state
505	    hash (more than one is an ambiguity the caller refuses to break). A
506	    state document carrying a bad marker value, or a marker without any
507	    binding sidecar, pairs with nothing.
508	    """
509	    pairs: List[RecoveryPair] = []
510	    for state_path, document, state_is_formal in state_cands:
511	        seq = _commit_seq_of(document)
512	        has_seq = COMMIT_SEQ_KEY in document
513	        try:
514	            mtime_ns = os.stat(state_path).st_mtime_ns
515	        except OSError:
516	            mtime_ns = -1
517	        marker = document.get(INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY)
518	        marker_present = INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY in document
519	        if not marker_present:
520	            if not formal_sidecar_present:
521	                pairs.append(RecoveryPair(
522	                    state_path, None, state_is_formal, False, seq,
523	                    has_seq, mtime_ns))
524	            continue

539	def _gate_integrity_sidecar(
540	        state_store: "JsonStateStore",
541	        document: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
542	    """Validate the marker/sidecar pairing of a loaded state document.
543	
544	    Returns ``(enabled, entries)``. A legacy document without the
545	    ``integrity_log_version`` marker and without a sidecar starts with
546	    ``(False, [])`` — the first write migrates it. Every other arrangement
547	    refuses startup with :class:`IntegrityLogError` and leaves both files
548	    untouched:
549	
550	    * marker present but sidecar missing, or vice versa;
551	    * a marker whose value is not the integer ``1``;
552	    * a sidecar that fails the structure/chain/hash validation, is empty, or
553	      whose last entry does not carry the document's generation and the
554	      document payload's canonical state hash.
555	    """
556	    marker_present = INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY in document
557	    try:
558	        log_document = _read_integrity_log(state_store.integrity_log_path)
559	    except IntegrityLogError:
560	        raise
561	    sidecar_present = log_document is not None
562	    if not marker_present and not sidecar_present:
563	        return False, []
564	    if marker_present and not sidecar_present:
565	        raise IntegrityLogError(
566	            "state document carries 'integrity_log_version' but the "
567	            f"integrity sidecar {state_store.integrity_log_path} is missing")
568	    if sidecar_present and not marker_present:
569	        raise IntegrityLogError(
570	            "an integrity sidecar exists beside a state document without "
571	            "'integrity_log_version'")
572	    marker = document[INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY]
573	    if not isinstance(marker, int) or isinstance(marker, bool) \
574	            or marker != INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION:
575	        raise IntegrityLogError(
576	            f"unsupported integrity_log_version marker: {marker!r}")
577	    entries = _verify_integrity_log(log_document)  # type: ignore[arg-type]
578	    if not entries:
579	        raise IntegrityLogError("integrity sidecar carries no entries")
580	    payload = {key: value for key, value in document.items()
581	               if key not in ("version", COMMIT_SEQ_KEY,
582	                              INTEGRITY_LOG_VERSION_KEY)}
583	    try:
584	        fresh = DeviceStore()
585	        fresh.restore_state(copy.deepcopy(payload))
586	        canonical = canonical_integrity_snapshot(fresh.snapshot_state())
587	    except (ValueError, TypeError) as error:
588	        raise IntegrityLogError(
589	            f"integrity sidecar state cannot be restored: {error}") from None
590	    expected_hash = integrity_state_hash(canonical)
591	    generation = _commit_seq_of(document)
592	    last = entries[-1]
593	    if last["commit_seq"] != generation:
594	        raise IntegrityLogError(
595	            "integrity sidecar last entry commit_seq "
596	            f"{last['commit_seq']} does not match the state document "
597	            f"generation {generation}")
598	    if last["state_hash"] != expected_hash:
599	        raise IntegrityLogError(
600	            "integrity sidecar last entry state_hash does not match the "
601	            "state document")
602	    return True, entries

701	    def save(self, state: Dict[str, Any], bootstrap: bool = False) -> None:

707	        ``.integrity-*.bak``) when they already exist, both temporaries are

722	        leaving both formal files untouched. After a replace has landed a
723	        failure rolls every replaced file back to its pinned inode (the first
724	        commit of a not-yet-existing file instead vacates the new snapshot:
725	        the state snapshot is quarantined, the sidecar deleted) and flushes
726	        the rollback with one more directory fsync. When that rollback cannot
727	        be completed durably — a rollback rename fails, or the second fsync
728	        fails — each restored inode is re-pinned as a ``.bak`` and its formal

854	    def _roll_back_transaction(self, directory: str,
855	                               plans: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
856	        """Undo landed renames after a failed two-file commit.
857	
858	        For every file whose replace landed, rename the pinned old inode back
859	        over its formal target (when there was no predecessor — the first
860	        commit creating that file — vacate the new snapshot instead: the
861	        state snapshot is quarantined, the sidecar deleted), then flush all
862	        rollback renames with one directory fsync.
863	
864	        Each plan ends with one of these outcomes:
865	
866	        * ``restored`` — the committed predecessor is authoritatively back
867	          on the formal path (and the rollback flush landed);
868	        * ``pinned-vacated`` — the formal path is missing and the committed
869	          predecessor survives pinned as a ``.bak`` (a failed rollback
870	          rename, or a rollback whose directory fsync could not be flushed
871	          and was therefore re-pinned and vacated);
872	        * ``new-vacated`` — a file that did not exist before the commit was
873	          removed again, so the formal path is correctly absent with no
874	          predecessor;
875	        * ``residual`` — an un-committed snapshot could not be taken off the
876	          formal path (undecidable).
877	
878	        When the rollback directory fsync fails, every ``restored`` inode is
879	        re-pinned under a fresh backup and its path vacated (becoming
880	        ``pinned-vacated``); an inode that cannot even be re-pinned simply
881	        stays authoritative as the committed content (the safe outcome).
882	
883	        The store ends *blocked* (durable marker) if any residual remains,
884	        otherwise *degraded* if a committed predecessor is missing from its
885	        formal path (a state ``new-vacated`` counts too — the first commit
886	        failed and the formal state is absent; a sidecar ``new-vacated`` is
887	        the correct pre-enable absence and never alone degrades), otherwise
888	        cleanly rolled back in place.
889	        """
890	        for plan in plans:
891	            if not plan["replaced"]:
892	                plan["outcome"] = "untouched"
893	                continue
894	            target = plan["target"]
895	            bak = plan["bak"]
896	            if bak is not None:
897	                try:
898	                    os.replace(bak, target)
899	                    plan["outcome"] = "restored"
900	                except OSError:
901	                    # The old inode stays pinned in bak; take the
902	                    # un-committed new snapshot off the formal path.
903	                    _vacate_target(directory, target,
904	                                   quarantine=plan["quarantine"])
905	                    plan["outcome"] = "residual" \
906	                        if os.path.exists(target) else "pinned-vacated"
907	            else:
908	                _vacate_target(directory, target,
909	                               quarantine=plan["quarantine"])
910	                plan["outcome"] = "residual" \
911	                    if os.path.exists(target) else "new-vacated"
912	        try:
913	            _fsync_directory(directory)
914	            rollback_durable = True
915	        except OSError:
916	            rollback_durable = False
917	        if not rollback_durable:
918	            for plan in plans:
919	                if plan["outcome"] != "restored":
920	                    continue
921	                # The rollback rename landed but its durability was not
922	                # flushed: re-pin the restored inode and vacate its path so
923	                # heal/startup face the decidable pinned-missing shape. When
924	                # even that is impossible the committed inode stays
925	                # authoritative (the safe outcome).
926	                if _repin_inode(directory, plan["target"], plan["prefix"]):
927	                    plan["outcome"] = "pinned-vacated"

929	        any_residual = any(plan["outcome"] == "residual" for plan in plans)
930	        any_pinned_missing = any(plan["outcome"] == "pinned-vacated"
931	                                 for plan in plans)
932	        state_new_missing = any(plan["outcome"] == "new-vacated"
933	                                and plan["quarantine"] for plan in plans)
934	        if not any_residual:
935	            # Pins of files whose rename never landed are redundant: their
936	            # formal targets never stopped holding the committed inode. Drop
937	            # them (best effort).
938	            for plan in plans:
939	                if plan["outcome"] == "untouched" and plan["bak"] is not None:
940	                    _remove_quietly(plan["bak"])
941	                    plan["bak"] = None
942	            try:
943	                _fsync_directory(directory)
944	            except OSError:
945	                pass
946	        if any_residual:
947	            # At least one formal path may still hold an un-committed
948	            # snapshot: never let it become authoritative. Persist the
949	            # blocking marker and refuse every later write until an operator
950	            # (or a verified pair) resolves it.
951	            _write_block_marker(directory)
952	            self.blocked = True
953	        elif any_pinned_missing or state_new_missing:
954	            # A formal path is missing with a pinned predecessor (or the
955	            # very first state commit failed): decidable, self-healing on
956	            # the next write.
957	            self.degraded = True
958	
959	    def heal(self, baseline: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
960	        """Self-heal the missing formal pair from pinned paired backups.
961	
962	        Called under the store lock by the persistence hook at the start of
963	        the next persist-able write after an undecidable write failure. The
964	        pinned *pair* is verified in full before promotion:
965	
966	        * the state backup (``.state-*.bak``/``.tmp``) must parse as
967	          version=1 at the immediately-previous generation, pass the whole
968	          cross-entity/cursor/nonce/audit-chain restore, and equal the
969	          process's last committed in-memory *baseline* exactly (the
970	          anti-dangling gate — a staged new snapshot can never equal it);
971	        * for a modern (``integrity_log_version``-stamped) state backup the
972	          sidecar backup (``.integrity-*.bak``/``.tmp``) must be the unique
973	          one whose hash chain verifies and whose tail binds that
974	          generation and the state's canonical ``state_hash``;
975	        * a legacy, marker-less state backup (the sidecar-enabling
976	          transaction was the one that failed) pairs only with *no* sidecar
977	          at all — the triggering commit re-anchors the chain afterwards.
978	
979	        Promotion is a same-directory *hard link* of each chosen backup, so
980	        the backup names keep pinning the inodes until the formal directory
981	        entries are fsync-durable. Only then are the same-transaction
982	        leftovers (redundant backups, staged ``.tmp`` snapshots, the
983	        un-committed ``.quarantine``) and any block marker removed.
984	
985	        A later write commit still goes through the normal atomic
986	        :meth:`save`, so healing consumes no generation: the healed commit
987	        advances ``commit_seq`` exactly once and carries only that triggering
988	        request — the earlier request that got 503 is never replayed.
989	
990	        Raises :class:`OSError` (mapped to 503/field=data_file by the caller)
991	        when no verifiable pair exists, two or more verifiable pairs exist
992	        (promotion is refused outright — choosing by name or mtime is
993	        forbidden), a formal file occupies a path without verifying, or the
994	        promotion cannot be made durable; in every such case the formal
995	        paths stay as they were, no leftover and no generation moves,
996	        :attr:`degraded`/`:attr:`blocked` stays set, and the next write
997	        retries this heal. A formal state file that verifies as the committed
998	        baseline always takes precedence over every backup (its missing
999	        sidecar may be restored from the unique matching sidecar backup); in
1000	        the *blocking* state an un-verified residual formal file is never
1001	        served and heal only unblocks once it is gone with one verifiable
1002	        pair (the durable ``.block`` marker is cleared then).
1003	        """
1004	        if not (self.degraded or self.blocked):
1005	            return
1006	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path))
1007	        state_leftovers = _leftover_tmp_paths(directory, self.path)
1008	        sidecar_leftovers = _sidecar_leftover_paths(
1009	            directory, self.integrity_log_path)
1010	        quarantined = _quarantined_paths(directory, self.path)
1011	        state_formal_exists = os.path.exists(self.path)
1012	        sidecar_formal_exists = os.path.exists(self.integrity_log_path)
1013	        expected_seq = self.commit_seq - 1
1014
